title: Provision Application Load Balancer
scenario: Your platform team needs Application Load Balancer for distributing HTTP traffic across targets. Write a reusable Terraform configuration that provisions it, drives every input through variables, applies the standard tags, and exports the operational identifiers.
constraints: Create exactly one resource of type aws_lb.
All configurable values must come from variables declared in variables.tf.
Code must pass terraform fmt conventions (2-space indents, trailing newline, no tabs).
Tag the resource with Project, Environment and ManagedBy = "terraform".

focus.title: Complete the aws_lb resource
focus.todo: Add the arguments and nested blocks required for aws_lb.

hints.why: A load balancer is the stable entry point in front of changing compute. Listeners and target groups define how traffic reaches the application.
hints.what: Complete the marked region in `main.tf`. The work is inside `resource "aws_lb" "this"`. Add the arguments and nested blocks required for aws_lb. Use the visible constraints as the checklist for names, values and references before you run the tests.
hints.when: Use a load balancer when traffic must be distributed, health-checked or terminated before reaching backend instances.
hints.how: Open `main.tf` and work only inside `resource "aws_lb" "this"`. Use this code shape: name; load_balancer_type; tags; subnets; security_groups; internal. Use the already-declared references instead of hardcoded values: `var.project_name`, `var.environment`, `var.subnet_ids`, `var.security_group_ids`. Keep the block header and braces, indent nested blocks by two spaces, and add one argument or nested block at a time. Run the tests after each small change so the first failure points at the next name to fix.
